title: Software Supply Chain Security & AI-Generated Code: Packages, Secrets, SBOMs & Signatures
concept: Protect a project from what it installs and what it ships: lockfiles and version ranges, packages an AI invented, typosquatting and dependency confusion, install scripts, secrets in code and logs, SBOMs you can diff, and artifacts verified against signed digests.
description: An advanced course for developers and DevOps engineers who own a CI pipeline. Every lesson starts from an incident on the CodeDev learning platform - a package an AI assistant recommended that did not exist until someone registered it, a scoped package the checker skipped, a postinstall script that read environment variables during the build, an API key printed by the config loader into CI logs, a release that shipped a dependency nobody added on purpose - and fixes it with a check you can automate: lockfiles and ranges, allowlists and package age, typosquat and slopsquat detection, dependency confusion, install scripts, secret scanning, SBOM diffs, digests and signatures, and CI token permissions. 12 lessons with True/False quizzes on real manifests, logs and SBOMs, and TypeScript challenges graded by hidden tests.

learningOutcomes.text: Explain typosquatting, slopsquatting, dependency confusion and malicious install scripts
Check lockfiles, version ranges, allowlists and package age automatically in CI
Find secrets in diffs and keep them out of logs
Generate and diff SBOMs and verify artifacts against signed digests
Limit CI token permissions and review AI-suggested dependencies before they land

knownIssues: No network in the code runner: registries, SBOMs and signatures are fixtures
